3/6 When you come forward in a #TimesUp &/or #MeToo story, you learn pretty quickly that publishing is not filled w/ legal wizards. 

The Seattle Times, for instance, had a film reviewer call my parents. (Mom is a retired attorney & Dad was Supervisor of the Sentencing Unit.)

5/6 All #TimesUp & #MeToo stories are unique.

In other ways, most of them share the same DNA.

You have to live in Seattle to realize just how Seattle-like parts of this story can be. (See: ostensibly progressive male artists not acting at all progressively.)

6/6 That said, I really am glad The Stranger finally updated the story. It feels like a huge weight has been lifted. 

Respect & solidarity to everyone of any gender who has come forward or is thinking of coming forward in a #TimesUp #MeToo story.

'Night, all. 

Peace.

2/2 Woody Allen con'td:

Lawyers know this. 

When you see companies finally take action, it's often b/c they've learned more than is in the public realm. 

Please remember that the number of persons actually harmed rarely aligns w the number you read. 

#TimesUp #MeToo

1/2 Re Woody Allen, so many of us who've come forward in #TimesUp #MeToo stories have made this point, but here we go again:

For every one of us who has come forward publicly, there are several more who've stayed off the record, on background, or who've stayed entirely silent.
